objective: Run a captured list of tasks sequentially, preserving exact results and stopping at the original failure.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Async/await and Promise sequencing are current language foundations.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Ordered operations and early failure are common application workflows.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Capturing membership and invoking work lazily transfers to pipelines.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Combines arrays, callbacks and awaited control flow at an intermediate level.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Live input changes or overlapping callbacks can execute unintended work.

defects: Reference/junior reread the caller array after awaits while the reduced senior captured initial callbacks.
Senior copied its growing results at each step, adding quadratic work.
Original failure/value identity, arity, snapshot membership and mutable-input policy were unspecified.
The live-input reference passed every previous assertion.
rationale: Choose and explicitly state initial membership, dense read-only/frozen arrays through 1000, exact zero-argument task calls and opaque values/reasons. Snapshot before any callback; all three boards now use a linear collection loop. Failure starts no later task. An initial microtask is allowed, so the producer gate is constructed externally and the first-start handshake also handles an unimplemented starter. Tests cover caller changes after invocation, synchronous/rejected Symbol reasons, frozen opaque values and fresh arrays, 1000 strictly sequential tasks and no later invocation while one task waits. Target linear total wrapper/snapshot/result work excluding callback work and scheduling; unknown source estimates retain 25 XP.

defects: Unique IDs, acyclic parent chains and the null sentinel were assumed but unstated.
Senior used a map constructor/array map instead of the requested two for-of passes.

rationale: Keep correct reference/junior, align senior to the explicitly requested passes, and define unique string/integer Map keys, no null IDs, acyclic existing-parent chains and read-only dense data records. Linear cost assumes average constant-time Map access and bounded keys, which is stated as the model rather than an ECMAScript guarantee.

objective: Coalesce IDs only within one first-timer batch and independently settle every caller across overlapping batches.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Closures, Map and Promise batching are current JavaScript patterns.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Batching data reads reduces repeated calls while retaining each caller result.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Gathering versus in-flight state transfers to queues and batching clients.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Combines timed closures and promise fanout after their foundations.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Accidentally retaining successful results can serve stale data or mix batches.

defects: Reference/senior Map iteration normalized -0 while junior passed raw -0 in a separate ID array.
Promise identity for duplicate calls and exact callback/result contracts were unstated.
A persistent successful-result cache passed all existing checks although each fired batch should be independent.
rationale: Retain reference and the valid senior shared-Promise form; normalize zero in junior to Map key behavior. Explicitly distinguish first timer gathering from fired/in-flight batches, no debounce/reset and no success/failure cache. Duplicate promises may be shared or distinct. Define stable read-only loadMany results, native Promises or synchronous throw, exact one-argument ID callback and opaque values/reasons, bounded keys/calls and Map cost assumptions. Cases request the same ID after success and while its old batch is pending, reenter during a throwing loadMany, inspect typed/prototype-like keys and canonical +0, and send 1000 calls/500 distinct IDs with no inline fetch. Total O(n) target counts calls plus sent unique IDs; factory scope remains unknown/25 XP under #410.

objective: Share a fresh cached Promise per opaque key and guard failed-request cleanup against replacing a newer entry.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Promise identity and cache invalidation remain current JavaScript concepts.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Concurrent widgets often reuse one in-flight data request.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Entry identity, expiration boundaries and guarded cleanup transfer to async caches.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: A supplied clock makes the intermediate race rules testable without real networking.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: A stale failure must not delete a fresh request or collapse distinct keys.

defects: Callback/clock domain, opaque key identity and zero TTL were unstated.
Hint said original Promise even though a stored rethrowing chain is also a correct cache implementation.
Stringifying keys passed the old all-string cases.
rationale: Keep all three functionally correct boards and specify the non-reentrant native-Promise producer, exact key argument, stable zero-argument nondecreasing supplied clock, TTL0 and equality expiration. Same fresh cache entry means exact stored Promise, without requiring producer-Promise identity. Preserve values/reasons and allow a cleanup chain that rethrows unchanged. New assertions check ten distinct typed/opaque keys, exact arity including -0/NaN, old failure after a replacement, fresh Promise for TTL0 and opaque values/undefined rejection fanout. The valid rethrowing-chain alternative is a permanent regression against over-restricting Promise identity. Target O(1) per get with average constant-time Map model; closure workload remains unknown/25 XP, not factory O(1) evidence.

objective: Maintain recency and eviction in a fixed five-entry cache while preserving the access sequence.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: LRU recency and insertion-ordered Set/Map remain current data-structure foundations.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Eviction policy is useful in bounded caches even though this exercise returns a serialized simulation.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Fixed capacity versus input-size scans teaches valid cost modelling.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: A five-letter simulation suits an introductory cache exercise rather than a production generic-cache API.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: It prevents basic recency, duplicate and input-mutation mistakes within this limited exercise.

defects: Input alphabet, size, read-only policy and cost variable were unstated.
An input-consuming shift implementation passed all existing checks.
rationale: Keep all three correct implementations, clarify uppercase ASCII letters/dense frozen input through 10000 accesses, fresh empty cache per call and least-to-most string output. Author O(n) time with O(1) retained cache, explicitly explaining that the junior inner scan and reference splice/shift touch at most five entries. Do not mislabel a bounded inner loop quadratic or replace the legacy API with an unrelated generic cache. Cases verify frozen input, independent repeated calls, empty state, 10000 cycling letters and 10000 duplicates; a Map alternative passes while destructive consumption fails. Unknown structural estimates keep 25 XP.
